scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

steps: read collection (AMI interval read or field manual read)
estimate substitution when no accepted read

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

H-REQ-FRAME.statement: Dispute ticket surge is due to insufficient response capacity; an AI agent to auto‑answer tickets would resolve the issue.

H-AMI-READ-LATENCY.statement: Delayed or missing AMI read exports cause estimation substitution, leading to incorrect bills and disputes.

H-FIELD-READ-DELAY.statement: Contracted manual meter reading delays or errors cause missing reads, leading to estimation and wrong bills.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: Recent changes to billing import validation rules introduced errors in bill calculation, causing wrong bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Dispute response times are within SLA (median 1.6 days < 3 days), indicating the surge in tickets is not due to slow response capacity.

The observation shows a substantial number of disputed bills stem from estimated reads (1240) versus actual reads (1785), indicating that estimation issues—such as missing AMI or field reads—are a significant contributor to the dispute surge, not merely response capacity.
The tariff change log shows no recorded tariff changes, indicating that tariff alterations are not contributing to the recent dispute surge or wrong bills.
Field route completion for August‑September is 0.88, below the target of 0.95, indicating delayed manual meter reads.
Dispute ticket counts rose from ~600 in June/July to >1,100 in August and >1,200 in September, showing a clear increase in dispute volume during the period of interest.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder SH-BILL states there has been no tariff change this year, indicating that tariff alterations are not a factor in the recent dispute surge.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder indicates a shortage of three manual meter readers since July has caused delayed routes, resulting in estimated bills for affected customers.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract confirms that the utility can request route priority changes, but such changes only take effect after confirmation by the Field Operations Manager.

structural_remedies.description: Increase field staff headcount by adding three manual meter readers via contract amendment with ORG-FIELD to eliminate the shortage that causes delayed routes.

structural_remedies.description: Request and obtain runtime confirmation for route priority changes (push_route_update) to prioritize delayed routes, ensuring higher completion rates for affected areas.
